site.intro.en.text: I'm a growth marketer on the creative side: I find out which ads and content actually drive installs and engagement, then scale them. I spent three years at HoYoverse, the studio behind Genshin Impact, running campaigns across North America, Europe and Japan. Lately I've been building my own AI tools to do it faster.

nodes.xbox-launch.summary.en.text: I led the creative strategy for Genshin Impact’s Xbox launch campaign across the US, France and Germany. The campaign delivered 120M+ impressions and lifted CTR by 338% against the benchmark.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.summary.en.text: I led the brand team's creative strategy for Genshin Impact's user acquisition, building a creator-led ad pipeline across Japan, North America and Europe. Our creatives delivered ~3.7× projected LTV and 26% higher projected 365-day ROI than the UA benchmark.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.sections.0.it.text: The UA team's tests showed creator ads scaled and converted well, but they couldn't produce enough of them. The brand team had creator resources but had never worked on user acquisition.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.summary.en.text: I scaled an early network of social channels for Zenless Zone Zero in Japan to 9 channels and 80M+ organic views, while cutting cost per view by more than 50%.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.team.en.text: Me (creative strategy, brand team), 1 UA strategist, 1 UA specialist and 4 agency partners. The UA team owned media buying and budget; I owned creative strategy and production.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.team.en.text: Me (social strategy), 2 content reviewers and 3 agency partners

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.sections.0.it.text: I had to build the Brand-to-UA pipeline from scratch and prove, within a few game updates, that our creatives could earn spend and bring in quality players, not just add volume. The budget only covered smaller creators, so the content itself had to do the work.

nodes.gip-testing.summary.en.text: I designed and ran a three-round test of TikTok’s UGC incentive programme as a UA channel. It delivered cheap reach, but acquisition and content quality weren’t stable enough to scale, so I recommended stopping it and moving the budget to creator ads.

nodes.xbox-launch.team.en.text: Me (creative strategy), 1 media strategist, 2 creative producers and 1 agency partner

nodes.influencer-activation.summary.en.text: I owned the creator strategy for a flagship Genshin Impact character event on X. The campaign delivered 13M+ views at 8%+ engagement, about 3× benchmark, at 39% lower CPM.

nodes.genshin-en-accounts.summary.en.text: Alongside our growth strategy lead, I shaped the strategy for 8 English-language Genshin Impact channels on TikTok and YouTube, refreshing the ones that had plateaued and building it from scratch for new ones. Together they drew 35M+ views and 64K+ new followers at about 30% below target CPM.

nodes.giveaway-campaign.summary.en.text: For a major Genshin Impact update, I led a giveaway with the biggest Genshin fan account on X, backed by 67 creators across X, TikTok and Instagram, to reach players beyond official channels. It drew 33M+ impressions and about 900K in-game code redemptions, 4× the goal.

nodes.interactive-filter.summary.en.text: For Lantern Rite, Genshin Impact’s Lunar New Year event, I co-developed two AR filters and briefed 70+ creators to kick off the trend as the campaign expanded from TikTok to Snapchat. It drew 600M+ views and 600K+ player videos, and the Snapchat Lens ranked #1 among sponsored Lenses.

nodes.landing-page.summary.en.text: For a major Genshin Impact update, I helped turn the launch landing page from an information page into a game: a short personality quiz with shareable results and a reward draw. It drew 9.5M+ unique visitors and 1.8M+ players into the draw, and converted 3× better than benchmark.

nodes.ua-creative-strategy.sections.1.it.text: Owned the testing framework: Translated acquisition goals into market-specific creative hypotheses, using performance data to steer tests across hooks, creative angles, scripts and formats.

Built the AI Creative Intelligence Dashboard: Used AI coding tools to create a dashboard that automates creative tagging and performance analysis, surfaces winning patterns and turns them into reusable scripts and playbooks.
Strengthened creator sourcing: Expanded regional talent pools through agency pitches and rotation, matching creators to the formats they perform best.
Directed creator production: Briefed creators, developed script templates and reviewed every video before launch.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.sections.0.items.a.text: The Zenless Zone Zero team asked the Genshin Impact brand team, given its social growth track record, to launch its Japanese channels and hand them over once they could run on their own. With little precedent for channels like these in Japan, I had to learn the market while testing what worked, then turn scattered experiments into a system another team could run, all on a fixed timeline.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.sections.1.items.a.text: Defined the channel strategy: Mapped Japanese player behaviour, competitor channels and content gaps to give each channel a niche with proven demand and clear content pillars across YouTube and X.
Ran biweekly growth reviews: Tracked every channel against its KPIs, diagnosed the ones falling behind and brought winning formats from other niches to stalled channels to restart growth.
Managed agency partners: Coordinated three agencies, aligning briefs, reviews and performance targets to lift content quality and cost efficiency.
Handed over a repeatable system: Codified content learnings, KPIs and routines into playbooks, and transferred all nine channels to the Zenless Zone Zero team.

nodes.zzz-jp-accounts.results.added-21cb.text: channels hitting view targets at handover

nodes.gip-testing.sections.0.items.added.text: Genshin Impact’s UA relied mainly on brand creatives. TikTok’s UGC incentive programme opened up a new possibility: could it boost installs efficiently as a UA channel, and could its videos work as UA creatives? I needed to design a testing framework to find out.

nodes.gip-testing.sections.1.items.added.text: Designed the test framework: Built a three-round roadmap, setting each round’s payout model (CPM or CPA), markets, themes, budgets and success metrics against our UA benchmarks.
Led campaign execution: Owned all three rounds end to end, from task setup and creator briefs to progress tracking, submission reviews and recaps.
Evaluated the channel and drove the decision: Measured reach, CPI, user quality and content relevance, then recommended stopping the programme and shifting budget to creator ads for UA.

nodes.gip-testing.results.added-c2840424.text: lower CPM in Round 3 than Round 1

nodes.xbox-launch.sections.0.items.added.text: The launch needed paid media to drive traffic to the Xbox landing page, not just awareness. That meant turning existing brand materials into 100+ localised assets, our team’s largest creative test for a paid brand campaign, with tight coordination across languages, platform specs and approvals.

nodes.xbox-launch.sections.1.items.added.text: Defined the creative strategy: Used past campaign learnings and regional player insights to build four testable creative concepts, adapted for US, French and German audiences.

Partnered on media optimisation: Shaped budget, regional priorities and targeting with the media strategist across YouTube, Meta, X and TikTok, then reviewed live results together to scale winners and pause underperformers.
Managed creative production: Wrote briefs covering copy, landing-page links and platform specs for all 144 assets, and kept timelines, reviews and approvals on track.

nodes.influencer-activation.sections.0.i.text: Engagement on Genshin Impact’s recurring character campaigns on X was flattening, and it was weakest among English-speaking players. Our previous creator campaign aimed for broad appeal: many of its creators reached general gaming audiences rather than core Genshin players, so it brought reach but under 3% engagement.
This time, I needed a creator lineup built around core players that would drive them to the official event on X and its in-game reward codes.

nodes.influencer-activation.sections.1.i.text: Set the creator strategy: Built the lineup around the artists, cosplayers, streamers and Genshin news creators that core players follow, so 80% of creators reached core players rather than general gaming audiences.
Localised for English-speaking players: Made English-language creators half the lineup and briefed a US agency on the art styles local players respond to.
Owned the full creator lifecycle: Ran budget, sourcing, briefing, timelines and approvals across two agencies, then benchmarked results to decide what to scale next.

nodes.giveaway-campaign.sections.1.items.text: Designed the campaign: Partnered with the fan account (1M+ followers). To enter, players quote-posted the giveaway with their own creative take, and in-game reward codes turned views into a measurable action.
Activated creators across platforms: Coordinated 67 creators across X, TikTok and Instagram, who posted their own entries first to show players how to join.

Led execution and the recap: Aligned four agencies on briefs, content review, timelines and tracking. Codes beat the goal, but fewer players entered because quote-posting a creative entry took too much effort. The lesson: fan-account giveaways need one-tap actions, like a repost or a reply.

nodes.genshin-en-accounts.sections.0.ite.text: Genshin Impact ran English-language social channels on TikTok and YouTube to keep players engaged between major updates. The established channels had stalled: formats were getting repetitive, fewer viewers were following and views dropped between updates. New channels needed a strategy built from scratch, all while keeping CPM under target.

nodes.genshin-en-accounts.sections.1.ite.text: Diagnosed what stalled growth: Benchmarked TikTok trends, competitor channels and each channel’s performance using Tubular and monthly reports, and pinpointed the gaps: too few evergreen topics, stale formats and weak follower conversion.
Refreshed the content mix: Shifted guide channels from patch-day tutorials to short, entertaining gameplay tips, so views no longer depended on update days.

Built strategy for the new channels: Set each channel’s audience, positioning, content pillars, formats and posting cadence from platform research, then refined them on early data before scaling production.
Ran monthly reviews: Tracked KPIs, reviewed English content and kept the agency’s output aligned with each channel’s growth goals.

nodes.interactive-filter.sections.0.item.text: Lantern Rite needed a social moment players could join, and this year the filter challenge was moving beyond TikTok to Snapchat for the first time. The filters had to be fun to use, simple enough for anyone to recreate, and right for two different platforms. We also had only a short window to build momentum and get the trend to take off.

nodes.interactive-filter.sections.1.item.text: Shaped the filter concepts: Researched competitor filters and co-developed two gesture-based ideas: releasing a sky lantern for TikTok and Snapchat, and a lion-mask transformation for a new character on TikTok. I wrote the creative briefs and reviewed each iteration with TikTok’s effects team.
Briefed creators: Turned each filter into simple video ideas for cosplay, beauty, pet, dance and transition creators, so their posts inspired players to make their own.
Vetted creators and content: Reviewed creator selection and videos for 70+ creators across TikTok and Snapchat, whose posts went live in the first week to kick off the trend.

nodes.landing-page.sections.1.items.adde.text: Benchmarked formats: Studied interactive web campaigns to find a mechanic with shareability built in.
Designed the hook: Chose a personality quiz, a proven viral format, so every player got a personalised result worth sharing, and kept it to three questions to cut drop-off.
Built the viral loop: Tied rewards to referrals. Finishing the quiz unlocked a reward draw and each friend invited earned another, so every share brought in about 4 new visitors.

nodes.landing-page.results.added-67b3312.text: players in the draw, +60% vs benchmark

nodes.ai-workbench.sections.0.items.0.en.text: AI tagging: Watches every video ad and tags its hook, format, pacing and more.

nodes.ai-workbench.sections.0.items.1.en.text: Winning formula: Links tags to performance data to show what top ads have in common, across updates and markets.

nodes.ai-workbench.sections.0.items.2.en.text: Script Studio: Turns the winning formula into new scripts, written natively for each market.

nodes.ai-workbench.sections.0.items.3.en.text: Campaign planning: Drafts the creative plan for the next campaign from past results.

nodes.ai-workbench.sections.0.items.4.en.text: Knowledge Base: Learns from every note, edit and piece of feedback, so results get sharper over time.

nodes.ai-workbench.headline.label.en.text: less time on creative analysis & production

nodes.ai-workbench.headline.note.en.text: I built it from scratch while running creative strategy for Genshin Impact's creator ads.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.0..text: Positioning: Benchmarked the top AI creators on Xiaohongshu and aimed the channel at AI beginners, promising that every video ends with something viewers can see and make themselves.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.1..text: Content formula: Compared my 73 posts with 35 viral posts from top AI creators. The winners led with the result, kept the barrier low and gave steps to follow, so that became the brief for every video.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.2..text: Test and scale: Kept testing new formats and topics, cut what didn’t convert, and doubled down on what worked.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.3..text: Content operations system: Built my own AI system that researches the platform and competitors, drafts scripts and runs biweekly growth reviews, so I can run the channel as a team of one.

nodes.xhs-ai-channel.sections.0.items.4..text: Brand partnerships: Partnered with China’s leading AI companies, including Alibaba’s Qwen, ByteDance’s Jimeng, MiniMax, Moonshot AI’s Kimi, LiblibAI and Lovart. Each sponsored video uses the product to solve a real task, not to list features.

nodes.creator-workbench.sections.0.items.text: Built on a proven workflow: Every module is a workflow I already run for my own channel, from research and viral-post breakdowns to scripts and growth reviews.
End to end: Takes content from research to idea, script, review and post-launch analysis in one place, instead of across chats, docs and spreadsheets.
Human in the loop: Agents research, analyse and draft, but nothing gets made until the creator picks the idea, and every draft stops for review.
Built for other creators: Helps new users set up their own content tags from a few sample posts, runs on the AI subscription they already pay for, and works in Chinese and English.
